narrative_summary: The market is in a Late Bull / Topping regime that has now failed its second recovery attempt: price closed 7,365.46 in the bottom third of the range, fully retracing the May-June advance and landing on the 61.8% fib / just above a flattening 50-day SMA with only a ~0.35% cushion. The mechanically intact bull skeleton (50d > 200d, +6.6% over the 200-day) is colliding with a zero-cushion ERP pinned at the 0.5% ceiling, Extreme Fear breadth and wide junk credit that have refused to confirm price for 8+ sessions, and a decisively down-first Monte Carlo edge (76.5%, 2-day median to downside) that fails every regime threshold. With ERP support now above spot and no capitulation washout to anchor a re-entry, defensive patience with a trim bias remains the only justified posture — sell strength into the 7,448-7,498 fib band, watch 7,351 as the acceleration trigger toward 7,199.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: The 50-day remains above a rising 200-day and price is still +6.6% over the 200-day, so the primary uptrend skeleton is mechanically intact and the decline could be a normal pullback within an ongoing bull.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: McClellan breadth (Extreme Fear, grinding to lower lows) and wide junk-credit spreads have refused to confirm price for 8+ sessions — classic narrow-leadership topping behavior that precedes the price skeleton breaking.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down.

conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A correction that unfolds without a volatility spike should be treated as orderly rather than capitulative; re-entry requires VIX reversing lower from an elevated reading.

primary_tension: A mechanically intact bull skeleton (50d > 200d, price +6.6% over the 200-day) is colliding with a failed second recovery attempt — a full retracement onto the 61.8% fib and flattening 50-day SMA, a distribution-style close, an ERP pinned at the 0.5% ceiling with valuation support now above spot, Extreme Fear breadth and wide credit refusing to confirm for 8+ sessions, and a 76.5% down-first Monte Carlo edge — leaving defensive patience with a trim bias, not re-entry, as the only justified posture.
